steps.label: Bounded-error Quantum Polynomial time
steps.sub: A polynomial-size quantum circuit that's correct with probability at least 2/3

steps.label: "Bounded-error" doesn't mean weak
steps.sub: Any fixed success rate above 1/2 is enough — the exact constant doesn't matter

steps.label: Error amplification makes 2/3 plenty
steps.sub: Run it k times, take the majority vote — wrong-answer probability shrinks exponentially in k

steps.label: "Polynomial" matches the classical bar
steps.sub: Circuit size grows polynomially with input size, same tractability line as P

code:
P      subset-of  BPP
BPP    subset-of  BQP
BQP    subset-of  PSPACE
BQP    subset-of  PP   (Adleman, DeMarrais, Huang, 1997)
caption: Quantum is proven at least as powerful as classical deterministic and randomized computing, and no more powerful than PSPACE.

steps.label: Factoring is in BQP and in NP ∩ co-NP
steps.sub: Shor's algorithm runs in poly time; a factorization is also quickly verifiable

steps.label: That overlap is a poor basis for a bigger claim
steps.sub: Factoring was chosen precisely because it sits in the overlap

steps.label: Grover's quadratic speedup is the best general NP tool
steps.sub: √N queries instead of N — still exponential overall on NP-complete search spaces

steps.label: BQP is not believed to contain NP-complete problems
steps.sub: No known quantum algorithm gives them an exponential speedup

subtitle: Sorting exponential, quadratic, and no speedup at all into their proper places.
